suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of feature-positive B cells for HLA-DR/DQ, CD83, and GPR183 surface expression, combined with functional assessment of antigen presentation capacity via mixed lymphocyte reaction with CD4+ T cells

programme_name: Early B-cell ribosomal translation and metabolic expansion
functional_description: This programme represents coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPL4, RPS2) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) in proliferating early B-cell stages (Large Pre-B, Pro-B Cycling, LMPP). The dominance of ribosomal machinery genes indicates heightened protein synthesis capacity required for rapid cell division and developmental progression, complemented by metabolic support genes (GAPDH, GPX1, UQCRH) providing energy and oxidative stress protection. The presence of CD74 and HLA-DRA reflects early MHC-II expression in developing B cells, though these are secondary to the primary translational programme.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17, RPL7A, RPL4, RPS2: Eight ribosomal protein genes dominate top-15 list—diagnostic of active protein synthesis machinery, not dendritic cell programme
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor—indicates active ribosomal elongation phase required for proliferating Pre-B and Pro-B cells undergoing rapid development
Cell-type composition (29% Large Pre-B, 20% Pro-B Cycling): Feature activates primarily in proliferative early B-cell stages requiring high translational demand
GAPDH, GPX1, UQCRH: Glycolytic and mitochondrial respiratory genes—support energetic demands of rapidly dividing lymphoid progenitors
CD74, HLA-DRA: Secondary MHC-II genes—present but not dominant; likely reflect incidental MHC-II expression during B-cell development, not a dendritic cell programme
suggested_validation: Perform polysome profiling or ribosome footprinting on sorted Large Pre-B and Pro-B Cycling cells vs mature B cells to quantify active translation rates and confirm the feature marks a translational expansion state rather than antigen presentation programme

programme_name: HLA-DP/DQ class II antigen presentation
functional_description: This programme represents coordinated upregulation of HLA class II molecules (DP and DQ heterodimers) and the chaperone CD74, enabling antigen presentation capacity in a subset of mature B cells. The co-enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS17, RPS23, RPS2, RPL37A, RPL4, RPL7A) suggests these B cells are actively synthesising MHC-II proteins to support immune surveillance, with FTH1 indicating elevated iron metabolism for biosynthetic demand.
key_evidence: HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1: DP heterodimer components diagnostic of non-canonical class II pathway, typically weaker than DR
HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1: DQ heterodimer components indicating broader MHC-II repertoire independent of DR
CD74: Invariant chain essential for HLA-II assembly, trafficking and peptide loading—present only in cells synthesising class II
RPS genes (RPS17, RPS23, RPS2, RPL4, RPL7A): Coordinated ribosomal upregulation indicates heightened translational capacity for MHC-II protein synthesis
FTH1: Iron storage protein upregulation reflects biosynthetic demand and potential ferroptosis resistance in antigen-presenting state
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of mature B cells for HLA-DP/DQ surface expression alongside CD74 intracellular staining, combined with quantitative mass spectrometry to confirm elevated MHC-II protein synthesis relative to total protein output; validate feature activation specifically in CD19+ HLA-II+ populations

programme_name: Large Pre-B cell proliferation and ribosome biogenesis
functional_description: This feature captures the translational machinery expansion programme active in large pre-B cells during rapid proliferation. The coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL7A), nucleosome-associated chromatin remodellers (HMGB1, HMGN1, HMGN2, H3F3A, H2AFZ), and translation factors (HNRNPA1, PPIA) reflects the biosynthetic demands of pre-B cell expansion prior to V(D)J recombination completion. This programme supports the synthesis of pre-BCR components and other developmental proteins required for proliferative expansion.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL7A: ribosomal structural proteins diagnostic of active translation capacity in rapidly dividing cells
HMGB1, HMGN1, HMGN2: chromatin architectural proteins enabling transcriptional accessibility during proliferative programme
PPIA: peptidyl-prolyl isomerase required for efficient protein folding under high translational flux
PTMA, STMN1: cell cycle regulators supporting proliferation (PTMA anti-apoptotic function; STMN1 microtubule dynamics)
SLC25A5: mitochondrial ATP/ADP antiporter sustaining energy demand during anabolic expansion
suggested_validation: Perform polysome profiling (sucrose gradient fractionation) on sorted large pre-B cells vs. small pre-B cells to confirm enhanced ribosome occupancy and active translation, coupled with pulse-chase labelling to quantify global protein synthesis rates.

programme_name: Early B-cell translational capacity programme
functional_description: This feature marks early B-cell progenitors (Pro-B, LMPP, Large Pre-B, HSC) with elevated ribosomal protein expression and translation machinery components, reflecting heightened anabolic demand during active proliferation and VDJ recombination. The programme is driven by coordinated upregulation of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPS2, RPLP0, RPS17) alongside translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), indicating preparation for rapid protein synthesis during cell cycle progression and lymphoid differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPS2, RPLP0, RPS17: Eight ribosomal protein genes dominating top-15 list diagnostic of high translational capacity in cycling progenitors
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor essential for efficient protein synthesis in proliferating cells
Cell-type composition: 35% Pro-B Cycling + 18% LMPP + 15.5% Large Pre-B = 68.5% actively proliferating early B-cell stages requiring maximal translational machinery
AIF1: Actin-binding protein induced by interferon; present in context of early progenitors suggests cytoskeletal reorganisation during proliferation
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein involved in pre-mRNA splicing; active during VDJ recombination and cell cycle transitions
suggested_validation: Sort Pro-B Cycling vs Pro-B VDJ cells by FACS (CD19+CD34+CD10+) and perform polysome profiling or quantitative mass spectrometry of ribosomal proteins and translation factors; expect significantly elevated polysome-associated ribosomes and higher incorporation of newly synthesized ribosomal proteins in cycling Pro-B cells relative to post-recombination stages.

programme_name: Ribosomal biogenesis and translation initiation
functional_description: This feature marks a coordinated programme of ribosomal protein synthesis and translational machinery assembly, predominantly active in HSCs and Large Pre-B cells. The dominant signal comprises 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4), translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), and nucleolar assembly factors (FBL), indicating active ribosome biogenesis. Supporting metabolic genes (TALDO1: pentose phosphate pathway for ribose-5-phosphate; FTH1: iron storage for iron-sulfur cluster assembly in ribosomal proteins) and chaperones (HSP90AB1) suggest this is a trans-acting programme enabling high translational capacity rather than a cell-type-specific differentiation state.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4: Six core 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins diagnostic of active ribosome biogenesis
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor GEF confirming functional translation initiation machinery assembly
FBL: Nucleolar small nuclear RNP required for rRNA 2'-O-methylation and ribosome assembly—marks nucleolar-active cells
TALDO1: Pentose phosphate pathway enzyme providing ribose-5-phosphate substrate for rRNA synthesis
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain enabling iron-sulfur cluster assembly in ribosomal proteins; marks cells with high iron turnover
suggested_validation: Sort top-activating cells (HSCs, Large Pre-B) by SAE feature 1958 activation level and perform qRT-PCR for RPS17, FBL, and TALDO1; confirm elevated ribosomal RNA and protein synthesis capacity by polysome profiling or puromycin-labelling FACS in high vs low feature-expressing subsets.

programme_name: Nucleocytoplasmic transport and chromatin remodelling during B-cell proliferation
functional_description: This programme reflects active nuclear-cytoplasmic dynamics in proliferating B cells (41% Mature B, 36.5% Large Pre-B, 13.5% Pro-B Cycling), driven by elevated nuclear import/export machinery (RANBP1), chromatin remodelling factors (HMGN2, H2AFZ, ANP32B), and actin polymerisation regulators (TMSB4X, STMN1). The co-expression of MHC class II presentation machinery (CD74, HLA-DRA) alongside snRNP components (SNRPG) and RNA-binding proteins (YBX1) indicates simultaneous transcriptional remodelling and antigen presentation capacity—hallmarks of activated or differentiating B cells preparing for clonal expansion or germinal centre entry.
key_evidence: RANBP1: Nuclear import/export adaptor essential for nucleocytoplasmic transport during active cell cycle progression
HMGN2: Marks transcriptionally active chromatin; co-expression with H2AFZ indicates chromatin remodelling in dividing cells
TMSB4X + STMN1: Actin/microtubule dynamics required for cell division and morphological changes in proliferating B cells
CD74 + HLA-DRA: Canonical MHC class II presentation genes, consistent with activated mature/large pre-B cells
SNRPG + YBX1: spliceosomal and RNA-binding proteins indicating active transcriptional remodelling during differentiation
MT-CO2: Elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation capacity in metabolically active dividing cells
suggested_validation: Perform RNA velocity or pseudotime analysis to confirm this programme marks B cells in active G1/S transition; validate RANBP1 and HMGN2 nuclear localisation by immunofluorescence in sorted Mature B and Large Pre-B populations; test whether RANBP1 knockout impairs pre-B to mature B transition kinetics

programme_name: MHC class II antigen presentation and B-cell activation
functional_description: This programme represents mature and immature B cells actively engaged in MHC class II-mediated antigen presentation and early activation responses. The coordinated upregulation of HLA-DP, HLA-DQ, HLA-DR, and HLA-DM molecules reflects B cells functioning as professional antigen-presenting cells, coupled with B-cell receptor signalling components (CD79A, BANK1) and co-stimulatory molecules (MS4A1/CD20, LTB). This is characteristic of activated B cells preparing for or engaged in T-cell help-dependent adaptive immune responses.
key_evidence: HLA-DPA1/DPB1, HLA-DQA1/DQB1, HLA-DRB1/HLA-DRA: Complete MHC class II presentation machinery; pentameric HLA gene co-expression is diagnostic of professional APCs
HLA-DMB: HLA-DM peptide-loading complex essential for functional MHC class II presentation; co-expression with HLA-D genes indicates active antigen processing
CD79A: B-cell receptor signalling chain; co-expression with MHC class II indicates BCR-stimulated activation state
BANK1: B-cell-specific scaffold protein amplifying BCR calcium signalling; marks activated B cells capable of receiving T-cell help
MS4A1 (CD20): B-cell pan-marker and co-stimulator; consistent with mature B cells in activated phenotype
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of feature-high B cells for HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ surface expression combined with phospho-PLCγ2 or phospho-SLP65 to confirm BCR signalling activation state; correlate with activated B-cell transcription factors (IRF4, STAT3).

programme_name: Early B-cell ribosomal biogenesis and translation initiation
functional_description: This feature activates a coordinated programme of ribosomal protein synthesis and translation machinery assembly during early B-cell development (Large Pre-B, LMPP, Pro-B cycling). The dominance of RPS and RPL genes (positions 1-7, 9, 14) coupled with translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPA1) indicates active ribosome biogenesis supporting rapid protein synthesis demands of proliferating progenitors. Supporting metabolic enzymes (TALDO1 pentose phosphate pathway for nucleotide synthesis, UQCRH mitochondrial respiration) and oxidative stress management (SOD1) sustain the biosynthetic energy requirements of this proliferative developmental stage.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS26, RPS17, RPS2: Multiple 40S ribosomal subunit proteins indicating active ribosome assembly
RPL37A, RPL4, RPL7A, RPLP0: 60S subunit proteins and acidic phosphoproteins required for functional ribosome
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor GEF activity enabling rapid protein chain extension in proliferating cells
HNRNPA1: hnRNP involved in mRNA processing and ribosome biogenesis coordination
TALDO1: Pentose phosphate pathway enzyme providing ribose-5-phosphate for rRNA and mRNA nucleotide synthesis
SOD1: Superoxide dismutase protecting biosynthetic machinery from ROS in high-metabolism progenitors
suggested_validation: Perform ribosomal biogenesis assay (pulse-chase rRNA labelling with ³H-uridine) comparing Large Pre-B and LMPP cells (high SAE51 activation) vs. mature B cells (low activation), predicting 2-3 fold increased ribosome assembly rate in feature-high cells. Confirm with qRT-PCR of pre-rRNA processing markers (45S pre-rRNA, ITS1/ITS2) and ribosomal protein mRNA abundance.

programme_name: Large pre-B cell mitotic chromatin remodelling
functional_description: This programme is activated in large pre-B cells undergoing active DNA replication and mitosis, characterised by upregulation of chromatin remodelling factors (HMGB1, HMGN1, HMGN2, H3F3A, H2AFZ) that facilitate transcription during S/G2/M phase, combined with microtubule polymerisation machinery (TUBA1B, TUBB) essential for mitotic spindle assembly and cytokinesis. The coordinated expression of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPLP0) and translation factors (PPIA) supports the protein synthesis demands of rapidly dividing cells, while PTMA and ANP32B provide apoptosis resistance and chromatin accessibility in proliferating lymphoid progenitors.
key_evidence: HMGB1, HMGN1, HMGN2: High-mobility group proteins that bind nucleosomal DNA and promote transcriptionally active chromatin—essential for gene expression during active cell cycle progression
TUBA1B, TUBB: α- and β-tubulin subunits forming microtubule heterodimers; diagnostic for cells in S/G2/M phases requiring spindle assembly and chromosome segregation
H3F3A, H2AFZ: Histone variants mediating chromatin remodelling and nucleosome displacement during transcription; hallmarks of proliferative chromatin state
RPS24, RPLP0, PPIA: Ribosomal proteins and prolyl isomerase indicating high translational capacity needed to support rapid protein synthesis in dividing cells
PTMA: Protamines and apoptosis inhibitors protecting dividing pre-B cells from DNA-damage-induced apoptosis during replication
suggested_validation: Sort BoneMarrowMap large pre-B cells by SAE feature 58 activation score; perform chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP-qPCR) for HMGB1/HMGN1 binding at replication-timing control regions (e.g. MCM2, CDC6 promoters) and validate microtubule polymerisation by immunofluorescence-based mitotic index quantification across feature-stratified populations

programme_name: B-cell antigen presentation and BCR signalling
functional_description: This feature represents the core B-cell identity programme, characterized by high expression of BCR complex components (CD79A, MS4A1/CD20), MHC class II molecules (HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, HLA-DP, HLA-DM), and B-cell-specific signalling scaffold proteins (BANK1). This programme is active in mature and immature B cells and reflects the fundamental capacity for antigen recognition, processing, and presentation to T cells.
key_evidence: CD79A: Essential component of B-cell antigen receptor complex; diagnostic BCR machinery gene
MS4A1 (CD20): Pan-B-cell marker and membrane-spanning protein defining B-cell identity
HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1: Complete MHC class II presentation machinery upregulation
BANK1: B-cell-specific adaptor protein essential for BCR-induced calcium signalling and B-cell activation
HLA-DMB: MHC class II peptide-loading molecule, required for functional antigen presentation
LTB: TNF family member involved in lymphoid organogenesis and B-cell survival signalling
CD74: Invariant chain for MHC class II assembly and trafficking
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of feature-positive B cells with anti-CD20, anti-CD79A, and anti-HLA-DR to confirm surface BCR and MHC-II expression; functional validation via in vitro antigen presentation assay using peptide-pulsed dendritic cells and feature-high vs feature-low sorted B cells

programme_name: Proliferative Pre-B chromatin remodelling and cytoskeletal dynamics
functional_description: This programme reflects the distinctive transcriptional and cytoskeletal state of actively proliferating Large Pre-B and Pro-B Cycling cells (76% of activated population). The coordinated upregulation of actin-sequestering proteins (TMSB4X, STMN1), HMG-box chromatin-binding factors (HMGB1, HMGN1/2, H2AFZ, PTMA, ANP32B), and core metabolic/proteasomal machinery (GAPDH, PSMA4, SLC25A5) indicates rapid chromatin remodelling coupled with microtubule/actin dynamics required during VDJ recombination and active proliferation. The enrichment of RNA-processing factors (HNRNPA2B1, LSM5, ERH) suggests concurrent transcriptional upregulation to support biosynthetic demand.
key_evidence: TMSB4X, STMN1: diagnostic for cytoskeletal remodelling during active cell division in proliferating Pre-B cells
HMGB1, HMGN1/2, H2AFZ, PTMA, ANP32B: coordinate chromatin accessibility and nucleosome positioning during VDJ recombination and gene expression bursts
GAPDH, SLC25A5, PSMA4: elevated glycolysis and proteasomal degradation reflecting metabolic acceleration in cycling Pre-B populations
HNRNPA2B1, LSM5, ERH: RNA processing capacity supporting transcriptional programme acceleration
suggested_validation: ATAC-seq or ChIP-seq (H3K4me3, H3K27ac) on FACS-sorted Large Pre-B and Pro-B Cycling populations to validate broad chromatin accessibility landscape; correlate with cell cycle phase (Ki67/PCNA) and VDJ recombination status (TdT expression) to confirm differentiation stage specificity.

programme_name: Large pre-B cell proliferative and DNA replication checkpoint
functional_description: This feature captures the transcriptional and translational machinery activation specifically in large pre-B cells undergoing active proliferation and S-phase progression. The coordinated upregulation of HMG-box proteins (HMGB1, HMGN1/2) with nucleosomal chromatin remodelling, combined with ribosomal proteins (RPS23/24, RPLP0) and translation factors (HNRNPA1/A2B1), reflects heightened transcriptional accessibility and protein synthesis demand during clonal expansion after successful VDJ recombination checkpoint passage.
key_evidence: HMGB1, HMGN1/2: High-mobility-group proteins enabling transcriptional opening and chromatin accessibility during active proliferation—diagnostic of cycling pre-B cells
STMN1: Stathmin microtubule dynamics regulator—critical for mitotic spindle function during active cell cycle in large pre-B cells
PTMA: Nucleosome assembly factor and apoptosis suppressor—essential for protecting proliferating pre-B cells from checkpoint-induced apoptosis
RPS24, RPS23, RPLP0: Ribosomal proteins reflecting elevated protein synthesis capacity needed to support rapid proliferation
HNRNPA1/A2B1: hnRNP splicing factors controlling alternative splicing of proliferation-associated transcripts (e.g., cyclin isoforms)
suggested_validation: Perform cell-cycle phase analysis (FUCCI or BrdU/EdU incorporation) stratified by feature activity in large pre-B vs pro-B cells, combined with chromatin accessibility assay (ATAC-seq) to confirm HMGB1/HMGN-mediated open chromatin at proliferation-associated loci (cyclin genes, replication licensing factors) specifically in activated feature+ large pre-B cells.

programme_name: BCR signalling and DNA damage surveillance in pre-B cells
functional_description: This programme reflects maturation checkpoints in pre-B cell development, characterized by active BCR signalling (CD79B, HCK Src-family kinase), heightened DNA damage surveillance and repair (NEIL1 base excision repair, HRK apoptotic licensing), and metabolic remodelling (ACSM3 fatty acid metabolism). The high frequency of Small Pre-B cells (35.5%) and mature B cells (48%) co-activating this feature suggests it marks the transition from VDJ recombination checkpoints toward functional BCR competence, with concurrent quality control mechanisms to eliminate cells with unresolved DNA damage.
key_evidence: CD79B: diagnostic BCR signalling co-receptor; directly required for pre-BCR and mature BCR function
HCK: Src-family kinase essential for BCR-mediated signal transduction and pre-BCR checkpoint signalling
NEIL1: base excision repair enzyme critical for resolving DNA damage incurred during V(D)J recombination
HRK: BCL-2 family pro-apoptotic member; mediates elimination of pre-B cells failing DNA damage checkpoints
FCRLA: Fc receptor-like protein implicated in B-cell survival and receptor editing during tolerance checkpoints
HLA-DMB: MHC class II component; marks developmental progression toward antigen presentation capacity
suggested_validation: Sort Small Pre-B and Immature B cells (CD19+CD10+); perform flow cytometry for phospho-HCK, phospho-SLP65 (BCR signalling) and γH2AX (DNA damage); cross-tabulate with cell cycle phase and apoptosis markers to validate coordinated BCR maturation with DNA damage surveillance.

programme_name: V(D)J recombination and early B-cell specification
functional_description: This programme represents the early stage of B-cell development characterised by active V(D)J recombination machinery (RAG2, DNTT) and pro-B specification factors (VPREB1, TCF4, MYB, SOX4). The dominance of Pro-B VDJ and Large Pre-B cells indicates active immunoglobulin gene rearrangement coupled with developmental transcription factor activity. Elevated DNA topoisomerases (TOP2B) and chromatin remodelling proteins (HMGN2) support the chromatin dynamics required for RAG-mediated recombination and transcriptional reprogramming.
key_evidence: DNTT: Template-independent polymerase essential for P/N nucleotide addition during V(D)J recombination
RAG2: Core V(D)J recombination endonuclease; diagnostic of active recombination-competent stage
VPREB1: Surrogate light chain component of pre-BCR; marks pro-B and pre-B developmental checkpoint
TCF4: E-protein transcription factor governing early lymphoid fate specification
MYB: Master regulator of pro-B cell identity and proliferation
SOX4: Co-regulator of B-lineage specification alongside TCF4
TOP2B: DNA topoisomerase required to relieve topological stress during active V(D)J recombination
HMGN2: Marks transcriptionally active chromatin at developmental regulatory regions
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting of RAG2+DNTT+VPREB1+ cells followed by single-cell RNA-seq and TCR/BCR sequencing to quantify actively rearranging V(D)J segments and correlate clonal diversity with developmental stage-specific gene expression patterns

programme_name: G2/M checkpoint and spindle assembly in proliferating B-cell precursors
functional_description: This feature marks cycling Large Pre-B and Pro-B cells in active mitosis, characterized by upregulation of microtubule dynamics proteins (TUBA1B, TUBB, NUSAP1), spindle checkpoint regulators (SMC4), and nucleosome remodelling factors (HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN1/2) required for condensed chromatin segregation. The co-expression of stathmin family proteins (STMN1) that destabilize microtubules and ubiquitin-dependent protein quality control (UBB) reflects the checkpoint surveillance mechanisms active during G2/M transition in rapidly dividing pre-B lymphocytes.
key_evidence: NUSAP1: diagnostic spindle microtubule organization protein, active specifically during mitotic spindle assembly phases
STMN1: stathmin-family microtubule catastrophe factor, marks cells in active microtubule turnover during M-phase
SMC4: structural maintenance of chromosomes protein essential for condensin-mediated chromosome segregation
HMGB1/HMGB2/HMGN1/2: high-mobility group proteins that remodel nucleosomal architecture during transcriptional silencing preceding mitosis
TUBA1B + TUBB: coordinate tubulin heterodimerization required for spindle pole organization and kinetochore-microtubule attachment
suggested_validation: Perform live-cell imaging of sorted Large Pre-B cells with fluorescent tubulin (GFP-TUBA1B) and spindle checkpoint markers (Aurora kinase B phosphorylation) to confirm NUSAP1/SMC4 co-localization at spindle poles and kinetochores during active mitosis; correlate feature activation with mitotic index via immunofluorescence for phospho-histone H3 (Ser10).

programme_name: Large pre-B cell proliferation and chromatin accessibility
functional_description: This programme coordinates cell cycle progression with dynamic chromatin remodelling in large pre-B cells undergoing rapid proliferation. The feature integrates microtubule/tubulin dynamics (TUBA1B, TUBB) essential for mitosis, nucleosomal DNA-binding proteins (HMGN1/2, HMGB1, DEK) that maintain transcriptionally permissive chromatin, and dNTP synthesis (TYMS) for DNA replication, alongside ubiquitin-mediated protein homeostasis (UBB) and cytoskeletal dynamics (STMN1) that stabilise microtubules during cell division.
key_evidence: TUBA1B/TUBB: α/β-tubulin heterodimers essential for mitotic spindle assembly and cytokinesis in rapidly dividing pre-B cells
HMGN1/HMGN2: nucleosomal DNA-binding proteins that maintain euchromatic architecture and active transcription during S/G2 phases
TYMS: thymidylate synthase catalyses dTMP synthesis from dUMP, rate-limiting for DNA replication in proliferating cells
HMGB1/DEK: high-mobility group proteins that facilitate chromatin remodelling and maintain supercoiled DNA topology during replication
STMN1: microtubule-destabilising protein that regulates dynamic instability during mitotic spindle formation
PTMA: prothymosin-α suppresses apoptosis in proliferating cells while enabling chromatin accessibility
suggested_validation: Co-stain large pre-B cells (CD10+, CD34+) with Ki-67 and HMGN1/HMGB1 by immunofluorescence to confirm chromatin accessibility markers co-localise with actively cycling cells; combine with BrdU pulse-labelling to phase cell cycle progression against SAE feature activation.

programme_name: Mature B cell antigen presentation and BCR signalling
functional_description: This programme represents a core mature B cell identity module, characterised by expression of pan-B cell markers (MS4A1/CD20), MHC class II molecules (HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1, HLA-DMB, HLA-DRB1), and BCR-proximal signalling machinery (HCK, BANK1). The enrichment in mature B cells (62.5%) with smaller contributions from early B cell stages indicates activation of this feature during late B cell development and antigen-responsive maturation, where B cells acquire full antigen presentation and BCR signal transduction competence.
key_evidence: MS4A1 (CD20): Pan-B cell surface antigen essential for B cell identity; diagnostic marker of mature B lineage
BANK1: B-cell-specific adaptor scaffold protein that couples BCR engagement to calcium signalling and immune activation—core BCR pathway component
HCK: Src-family kinase preferentially expressed in B lineage; phosphorylates BCR-associated proteins (Syk, Blnk) to initiate signal cascade
HLA-DQA1/HLA-DQB1/HLA-DMB/HLA-DRB1: MHC class II molecular components enabling antigen presentation; coordinately expressed during mature B cell differentiation
LTB: TNF superfamily member supporting lymphocyte-endothelial interactions and tissue homing; marks B cells in organised lymphoid microenvironments
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for CD20+, HLA-DR+, and phospho-BANK1 (pY402) stimulated with anti-IgM to confirm that mature B cells activating this SAE feature show heightened BCR-proximal phosphorylation and sustained MHC class II expression relative to pre-B or immature B cells.

programme_name: Pro-B cycling and mitotic checkpoint control
functional_description: This feature represents active cell cycle progression and mitotic spindle organization in proliferating pro-B cells. The programme is characterized by upregulation of microtubule dynamics regulators (STMN1, TUBB, TUBA1B, NUSAP1), nucleolar-associated proteins involved in ribosome biogenesis (HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2), and core mitotic machinery (SMC4, MKI67). This reflects the heightened biosynthetic and mitotic activity of pro-B cells undergoing rapid proliferation prior to VDJ recombination.
key_evidence: STMN1: Stathmin regulates microtubule dynamics and is essential for proper spindle checkpoint function during mitosis
NUSAP1: Nucleolar-spindle-associated protein directly organizes spindle microtubules and is a canonical cell cycle phase marker
MKI67: Ki-67 proliferation antigen is obligatory for mitotic progression and marks actively cycling cells
HMGB1/HMGB2: Non-histone chromosomal proteins associated with transcriptionally active chromatin during high biosynthetic demand
TUBB/TUBA1B: Tubulin heterodimer subunits required for centrosome organization and mitotic spindle assembly
SMC4: Structural maintenance of chromosomes protein necessary for chromatin condensation during mitosis
suggested_validation: Co-stain sorted pro-B cycling cells with NUSAP1, STMN1, and phospho-histone H3 by immunofluorescence to confirm co-localization at spindle poles and metaphase plates during active mitosis; validate with BrdU pulse-chase to confirm enrichment in S/G2/M phases

programme_name: Large pre-B ribosomal assembly and translational capacity
functional_description: This programme represents coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S subunits: RPS24, RPS17, RPS2, RPS23, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPL37A) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) in large pre-B cells, indicating rapid ribosome biogenesis to support the translational burst required for pre-B cell receptor (pre-BCR) signalling and subsequent clonal expansion. Co-expression of nucleosome-associated proteins (HMGN1, HMGB1) and translation cofactors (PPIA, YBX1) suggests coordinated transcriptional activation and translational initiation machinery engagement during the proliferative pre-B stage.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS17, RPS2, RPS23, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPL37A: Multiple ribosomal protein subunits (40S and 60S) diagnostic of ribosomal assembly burst
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor indicating global translational capacity upregulation
PPIA: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase essential for efficient ribosome function and protein folding during high-rate translation
HMGN1, HMGB1: Chromatin-associated proteins facilitating transcriptional activation of ribosomal genes and translation machinery
YBX1: RNA-binding protein regulating translation initiation and mRNA stability during proliferative phase
suggested_validation: Measure polysome abundance and actively translating ribosome density in large pre-B vs. small pre-B cells by polysome profiling or flow-based ribosome quantification; correlate with pre-BCR signalling markers (CD79B phosphorylation, ERK1/2 activation) to confirm translational burst timing

programme_name: Large Pre-B chromatin remodeling and actin dynamics
functional_description: This programme is activated specifically in Large Pre-B cells and represents active chromatin remodeling coupled with cytoskeletal reorganization during the proliferative pre-B stage. The coordinated upregulation of nucleosomal architecture proteins (HMGB1, HMGN1/2, H2AFZ, H3F3A) with actin regulators (TMSB4X, STMN1) and RNA processing factors (HNRNPA1/A2B1) indicates simultaneous transcriptional activation and cytoplasmic remodeling required for rapid cell division and large cell morphology.
key_evidence: HMGB1, HMGN1/2: Nucleosomal DNA binding and transcriptionally active chromatin markers—diagnostic for open chromatin state in proliferating Pre-B cells
H2AFZ, H3F3A: Histone variants incorporated during active chromatin remodeling and DNA replication
TMSB4X: Actin sequestering protein essential for cytoskeletal dynamics during cell growth and mitosis
STMN1: Microtubule-destabilizing phosphoprotein required for mitotic progression and morphological expansion
HNRNPA1/A2B1, ANP32B: RNA processing and histone binding factors supporting high transcriptional output during proliferation
suggested_validation: FACS sort Large Pre-B (CD19+CD34+CD10+CD20-) vs Pro-B and Mature B cells, perform ATAC-seq to confirm open chromatin at enhancers associated with cell cycle and actin regulators, and validate TMSB4X and STMN1 phosphorylation status as markers of pre-B mitotic activity

programme_name: Large Pre-B cell G1/S checkpoint ribosomal biosynthesis
functional_description: This programme represents the coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPLP0, RPS17, RPS23) and chromatin-associated nucleolar organiser proteins (HMGB1, HMGN1, HMGN2, H2AFZ, ANP32B) in large Pre-B cells, reflecting active rRNA synthesis and ribosome biogenesis required for imminent cell cycle entry. The concurrent expression of microtubule regulators (STMN1, TMSB4X) and RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPA1, HNRNPA2B1, PTMA) indicates coordination of translation machinery assembly with G1/S phase progression and nuclear reorganisation.
key_evidence: HMGB1, HMGN1, HMGN2: High-mobility-group nucleolar proteins that organise rDNA and facilitate ribosome biogenesis—diagnostic of pre-ribosomal assembly
RPS24, RPLP0, RPS17, RPS23: Ribosomal protein structural components—indicate active ribosome biogenesis during G1/S transition in proliferating Pre-B cells
STMN1, TMSB4X: Microtubule catastrophe and actin dynamics regulators—essential for mitotic spindle formation during Large Pre-B proliferation
HNRNPA1, HNRNPA2B1, PTMA: RNA-binding and chromatin proteins promoting transcriptional elongation and anti-apoptotic signalling—coordinate with ribosomal rRNA transcription
suggested_validation: Perform sequential FACS/RNA-FISH on sorted Large Pre-B cells: quantify S-phase entry (BrdU incorporation) correlated with RPS24/RPLP0 expression; validate rRNA synthesis by pulse-labelling with [³H]-uridine; confirm nucleolar accumulation of HMGB1/HMGN1 by immunofluorescence to establish causality between ribosomal biosynthesis and G1/S checkpoint transit.

programme_name: Mature B cell antigen presentation and BCR signalling
functional_description: This programme represents coordinated upregulation of HLA class II molecules (DR, DQ, DP, DM), B-cell identity markers (MS4A1/CD20, CD79A, BANK1), and lymphotoxin signalling in mature B cells. The feature captures the characteristic transcriptional state of antigen-presenting B cells with competent BCR signalling machinery and MHC class II-mediated immune cooperation.
key_evidence: CD74: invariant chain essential for HLA class II assembly and trafficking - diagnostic of professional APCs
HLA-DRA/DRB1/DQA1/DQB1/DPA1/DPB1: complete HLA class II heterodimer complex - hallmark of B cell antigen presentation capacity
MS4A1: B-cell-specific tetraspanin marker (CD20) - defines mature B cell identity
CD79A: BCR signalling component - required for B cell activation and antigen responsiveness
BANK1: B-cell scaffold protein for BCR-induced calcium signalling - essential for signal transduction
LTB: TNF family member mediating lymphocyte-stroma interactions - supports B cell survival and activation
HLA-DMB: MHC class II peptide-loading catalyst - optimizes antigen presentation efficiency
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of HLA-DR + CD20 + CD79A on mature B cells from bone marrow to confirm coordinated surface expression, combined with functional assay of antigen uptake and presentation capacity in sorted HLA-DR+ B cells

programme_name: Metabolic stress adaptation and ER proteostasis
functional_description: This programme is active in proliferating pre-B and plasma cells undergoing intensive protein synthesis, characterised by coordinated upregulation of antioxidant enzymes (SOD1, PRDX2, GLRX), ER protein disulfide isomerases (PDIA6, P4HB), and ribosomal proteins (RPLP0, RPL37A). The co-expression of ubiquitin (UBB), DAD1 (apoptosis suppression), and BSG suggests concurrent management of proteotoxic stress through both ER-assisted folding and selective protein degradation pathways to maintain cellular viability during high-demand synthetic states.
key_evidence: PDIA6 & P4HB: Catalytic ER protein disulfide isomerases essential for Ig heavy/light chain pairing during synthesis
SOD1, PRDX2, GLRX: Redox scavenging enzymes controlling ROS generated by high mitochondrial activity in proliferating/secretory cells
RPLP0, RPL37A: Ribosomal proteins reflecting intensive translation load in pre-B (VDJ recombination, cell cycle) and plasma cells (antibody synthesis)
UBB & DAD1: Ubiquitin-proteasome system activation combined with apoptosis suppression, indicating proteotoxic stress management
BSG: Metabolite transporter supporting rapid glucose/lactate flux during anabolic phases of differentiation
suggested_validation: Perform oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) measurements on FACS-sorted Feature528-high Large Pre-B and plasma cells vs Feature528-low cells; assess ER lumen ROS using TMRM staining and correlate with PDIA6/P4HB protein levels by flow cytometry.

programme_name: Ribosomal protein synthesis and chromatin remodelling in proliferating pre-B cells
functional_description: This feature represents coordinated upregulation of ribosomal structural proteins (RPS24, RPLP0, RPS17, RPS23, RPL37A) and nucleosome-associated chromatin remodelling factors (HMGN1, HMGN2, HMGB1) in large pre-B cells undergoing active proliferation. The gene signature indicates simultaneous ribosome biogenesis and transcriptional activation of the chromatin landscape, supporting rapid protein synthesis and cell cycle progression characteristic of the large pre-B stage.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS17, RPS23, RPLP0, RPL37A: Multiple ribosomal protein subunits diagnostic of active ribosome assembly and translational capacity in proliferating cells
HMGN1, HMGN2, HMGB1: HMG-box chromatin remodellers associated with transcriptionally active chromatin required for cell cycle gene expression
PTMA, STMN1: Anti-apoptotic and microtubule dynamics regulator supporting proliferation survival and mitotic progression
HNRNPA1, HNRNPA2B1: Pre-mRNA processing factors coordinating splicing with rapid transcription during S-phase
suggested_validation: Perform polysome profiling on sorted large pre-B cells (76% of feature activators) vs. other B-cell stages to confirm elevated polysome accumulation and active translation initiation rate; correlate with cell cycle phase (Ki-67/DAPI) to validate S/G2-M phase enrichment.

programme_name: MHC class II antigen presentation and B-cell receptor signalling
functional_description: This programme represents mature and immature B cells with active antigen presentation capacity and B-cell receptor signalling competence. The coordinated upregulation of HLA class II molecules (DR, DQ, DP, DM) alongside B-cell identity markers (MS4A1/CD20, CD79A, BANK1) and lymphotoxin-beta indicates B cells engaged in professional antigen presentation and bystander activation, characteristic of activated or memory B-cell populations in lymphoid niches.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1: Complete HLA-DR and HLA-DP heterodimer assembly for peptide-MHC presentation
HLA-DMB, HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1: HLA-DM chaperone and HLA-DQ molecules for MHC class II peptide loading
CD74: Invariant chain essential for MHC class II trafficking and peptide loading in endosomal compartments
MS4A1 (CD20) + CD79A + BANK1: B-cell lineage markers with BCR signalling scaffold proteins confirming B-cell identity
LTB + GPR183: Lymphotoxin signalling and EBV-induced activation marker indicating activated B-cell state
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining: CD20+ cells should show high HLA-DR/DQ surface expression with elevated CD79A and BANK1 protein levels; functional validation via stimulation with cognate antigen to confirm enhanced antigen presentation capacity and proliferation compared to HLA-DR-negative B-cell subsets

programme_name: Ribosomal protein synthesis and HSC quiescence maintenance
functional_description: This feature captures coordinated upregulation of ribosomal structural proteins (40S and 60S subunit components) and translation factors in long-term HSCs and LMPPs, reflecting active ribosome biogenesis machinery. The concurrent expression of oxidative stress response genes (GPX1, GSTP1) and the nucleolar protein NPM1 suggests a programme balancing metabolic self-renewal capacity with protection against proteotoxic stress during quiescent HSC maintenance rather than active B-cell differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS26, RPS24, RPS23, RPS17: Multiple 40S ribosomal protein subunit genes—diagnostic for ribosomal assembly, not B-cell lineage specification
RPL37A, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPL4: 60S ribosomal subunit components—comprehensive ribosome biogenesis signature independent of B-cell state
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor—supports active protein synthesis machinery, characteristic of metabolically active but non-differentiating progenitors
NPM1: Nucleolar protein involved in ribosome assembly and stress response—enriched in HSCs with active ribosomal protein synthesis
GPX1, GSTP1: Oxidative stress defence enzymes—protect metabolically active HSCs/LMPPs during ribosome biogenesis from ROS-induced damage
suggested_validation: Co-stain HSCs and LMPPs for ribosomal protein expression (RPL4 or RPS26) with metabolic dyes (MitoTracker, pyronin) and HSC markers (CD150, CD48) to confirm this programme marks quiescent HSCs with active ribosome biogenesis capacity but low protein translation output, distinct from cycling progenitors or differentiated B cells

programme_name: Cell cycle progression and mitotic spindle assembly
functional_description: This programme coordinates tubulin polymerization (TUBA1B, TUBB), deoxyribonucleotide synthesis (TYMS), and chromatin remodeling during active pre-B cell proliferation. The enrichment of histone variants (H3F3A, H2AFZ, H2AFY, H2AFV), microtubule stabilization (STMN1), and mitotic checkpoint proteins (DEK, PCLAF) reflects synchronized DNA replication and mitotic spindle assembly in large pre-B cells undergoing VDJ recombination-coupled expansion.
key_evidence: TUBA1B, TUBB: Essential structural components of mitotic spindles and microtubule networks required for cytokinesis in rapidly dividing pre-B cells
TYMS: Rate-limiting enzyme for deoxyribonucleotide biosynthesis; diagnostic marker of S-phase cells undergoing DNA replication
STMN1: Microtubule-destabilizing phosphoprotein that regulates spindle dynamics and checkpoint control during mitosis
H3F3A, H2AFZ, H2AFY, H2AFV: Histone variants incorporated into chromatin during active transcription and replication in cycling cells
DEK, PCLAF: Chromatin-binding proteins involved in mitotic progression and chromosome condensation
HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN2, PTMA: High-mobility group proteins that facilitate chromatin accessibility during active transcription in S/G2-phase cells
suggested_validation: Co-stain large pre-B and pro-B cycling cells with Ki-67 (proliferation) and α-tubulin (spindle assembly) immunofluorescence, then perform live-cell time-lapse microscopy to confirm active mitosis and spindle checkpoint dynamics in SAE feature 799+ cells.

programme_name: MHC class II antigen presentation and B-cell activation
functional_description: This programme reflects mature and immature B cells with heightened MHC class II expression and BCR-mediated signalling competence. The coordinated upregulation of HLA class II molecules (DPA1, DRB1, DQA1, DQB1, DPB1, DRA, DMB), the invariant chain CD74, and B-cell receptor components (CD79A, MS4A1/CD20) indicates active antigen-presenting capacity coupled with BCR signalling readiness. BANK1 scaffold protein and GPR183 (EBV-responsive gene) further support a B-cell state primed for immune activation and antigen recognition.
key_evidence: CD74: Invariant chain essential for MHC class II assembly and peptide loading in the ER-Golgi pathway
HLA-DPA1/DRB1/DQA1/DQB1/DPB1/DRA/DMB: Complete HLA class II heterodimerisation machinery required for professional antigen presentation
CD79A: B-cell receptor signal transduction component; upregulation indicates BCR priming
BANK1: B-cell-specific scaffold protein for BCR-induced calcium signalling and immune synapse formation
MS4A1 (CD20): Pan-B-cell marker with regulatory role in BCR signalling threshold
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of cells with high feature 850 activation for HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, CD79A, and CD20 surface expression, combined with calcium flux assay upon BCR crosslinking to confirm enhanced signalling competence

programme_name: MHC class II antigen presentation and B-cell activation
functional_description: This programme represents mature and immature B cells with elevated MHC class II molecule expression (HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, HLA-DP, HLA-DM) coupled with core B-cell receptor signalling machinery (CD79A, BANK1) and lymphoid homing factors (LTB, GPR183). The coordinated upregulation of antigen-processing molecules (CD74, HLA-DMB) alongside BCR components indicates activated B cells engaged in antigen presentation and T-cell cooperation, typical of germinal centre-experienced or activated mature B cells.
key_evidence: CD74: MHC class II invariant chain; essential for HLA-DQ/DP assembly and antigen loading—diagnostic of professional antigen-presenting B cells
HLA-DRA/DRB1/DQA1/DQB1/DPA1/DPB1: Complete HLA class II heterodimer expression (all three classical complexes) indicates heightened antigen presentation capacity beyond resting B cells
CD79A + BANK1: B-cell receptor signalling scaffold proteins; co-expression with MHC-II suggests tonic BCR engagement or recent antigen stimulation
HLA-DMB: Peptide exchange factor for HLA-DQ/DP; indicates active antigen processing, not passive MHC-II expression
MS4A1 (CD20): Stable B-cell marker confirming B-cell identity; high expression consistent with mature B-cell subset
LTB + GPR183: Lymphoid tissue homing and EBV-induced activation markers; suggest cells positioned for T-cell interaction in secondary lymphoid tissues
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD19+ B cells for HLA-DR, HLA-DQ, CD79b, and Ki-67, combined with phospho-flow for BCR signalling (pSyk, pLyn) to confirm that high MHC-II expressers are proliferating, recently antigen-stimulated B cells in secondary lymphoid compartments rather than resting naive cells.

programme_name: MHC-II antigen presentation priming in cycling B precursors
functional_description: This programme activates HLA class II antigen presentation machinery (HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DPA1, CD74) specifically in Pro-B cycling and Large Pre-B cells during early B-cell development. Concurrent expression of chromatin remodelling factors (HMGB1, HMGN1, HMGN2, H3F3A) and cytoskeletal regulators (TMSB4X, STMN1) indicates coordinated preparation for MHC-II-mediated antigen presentation coupled with active proliferation and nuclear reorganisation.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA/DRB1/DPA1: Complete HLA class II presentation complex assembly—diagnostic of antigen presentation-competent B cells
CD74: Invariant chain chaperone required for HLA class II trafficking and peptide loading—confirms functional presentation machinery
HMGB1, HMGN1, HMGN2: High-mobility group proteins that remodel chromatin at active loci—indicate transcriptional permissiveness for MHC-II genes
TMSB4X, STMN1: Actin and microtubule dynamics regulators—support vesicular trafficking of MHC-II complexes during active proliferation
H3F3A, PPIA: Histone chaperone and prolyl isomerase—facilitate nucleosome remodelling at MHC-II loci and ER protein folding
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry with HLA-DR surface staining co-gated with Ki67 (proliferation) and CD34/CD19 markers to confirm MHC-II expression is enriched in cycling Pro-B and Pre-B populations; ATAC-seq on sorted Pro-B to validate open chromatin at HLA class II loci.

prior_zero_shot_name: Progenitor cell proliferation and RNA processing
programme_name: Large pre-B cell S-phase chromatin remodelling
functional_description: This programme represents the coordinated upregulation of histone variants (H3F3A, H2AFZ, H2AFV), nucleosome-binding architectural proteins (HMGB1, HMGB2, HMGN1, HMGN2), and microtubule/mitotic machinery (TUBA1B, TUBB, STMN1) during active DNA synthesis in large pre-B cells. The enrichment of nucleosome remodelling factors (DEK, ANP32B) alongside DNA replication enzymes (TYMS) and ubiquitin (UBB) indicates coordinated chromatin accessibility maintenance and protein turnover during rapid G1/S progression.
key_evidence: HMGB1/HMGB2/HMGN1/HMGN2: Non-histone chromosomal proteins that facilitate transcriptionally-permissive chromatin architecture during S-phase
H3F3A/H2AFZ/H2AFV: Histone variants incorporated during active DNA replication to maintain open chromatin and transcriptional competence
TUBA1B/TUBB/STMN1: Microtubule dynamics and spindle checkpoint machinery essential for mitotic progression in cycling pre-B cells
TYMS: Thymidylate synthase for dTMP synthesis, diagnostic of active DNA replication
DEK/ANP32B: Chromatin-binding proteins that facilitate nucleosome remodelling and histone acetylation during transcriptional activation
suggested_validation: Sort large pre-B cells by Feature 1150 activation level, perform cell-cycle phase analysis (BrdU/DAPI or Ki67/phospho-histone H3), and measure chromatin accessibility by ATAC-seq to confirm enhanced nucleosome dynamics in S-phase populations

programme_name: Pre-B cell ribosomal protein synthesis and chromatin remodelling
functional_description: This programme is specifically active in Large Pre-B and Pro-B cycling cells, characterized by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPLP0, RPS24, RPS17, RPS23) paired with chromatin-associated nucleosome-binding proteins (HMGB1, HMGN1, HMGN2, H2AFZ). This reflects the intense biosynthetic demand and open chromatin state required for active VDJ recombination and rapid cell cycle progression in pre-B cell development, rather than generic translational elongation.
key_evidence: HMGB1, HMGN1, HMGN2, H2AFZ: Nucleosomal DNA-binding proteins associated with transcriptionally active chromatin permissive for RAG recombination
RPLP0, RPS24, RPS17, RPS23: Ribosomal protein components diagnostic of high protein synthesis capacity during rapid proliferation
STMN1, TMSB4X: Cytoskeletal regulators (microtubule destabilization and actin sequestering) supporting mitotic spindle dynamics during cell cycle
HNRNPA1, HNRNPA2B1: hnRNP splicing regulators enabling rapid, coordinated pre-mRNA processing in proliferative progenitors
PTMA, ANP32B: Nuclear matrix proteins supporting transcription factor accessibility during VDJ recombination
suggested_validation: Sort Large Pre-B and Pro-B cycling cells by SAE feature 1202 activation; perform ChIP-seq for RAG1/RAG2 and H3K4me3 on high vs low feature expressers to confirm open chromatin accessibility, paired with metabolic labelling (O-propargyl-puromycin) to quantify ribosomal protein synthesis rates.

programme_name: Proliferative chromatin remodelling and cell cycle progression
functional_description: This programme activates in cycling Pro-B and large Pre-B cells and is driven by coordinated upregulation of nucleosomal architecture proteins (HMGB1/2, HMGN1/2, H2AFZ, H3F3A) that maintain transcriptionally permissive chromatin during rapid DNA replication. Co-expression of microtubule dynamics regulators (STMN1, TUBA1B), anti-apoptotic factors (PTMA), and RNA processing factors (HNRNPA2B1/A3) coordinates G1/S transition, mitotic progression, and global translation during the high biosynthetic demand of B-cell precursor expansion.
key_evidence: HMGN2, HMGN1, HMGB1, HMGB2: Non-histone chromosomal proteins that maintain nucleosome dynamics and transcriptional accessibility during active replication
STMN1, TUBA1B: Microtubule/mitotic spindle regulation essential for cell cycle progression in rapidly dividing Pro-B and Pre-B cells
H2AFZ, H3F3A: Histone variants enriched at regulatory regions and replacing canonical histones during active transcription
PTMA: Apoptosis antagonist preventing programmed cell death during vulnerable S/G2 phases
HNRNPA2B1, HNRNPA3: hnRNPs mediating alternative splicing and mRNA stability of cell cycle checkpoint genes
suggested_validation: FACS-sort Pro-B Cycling and Large Pre-B cells by Ki67/BrdU incorporation and perform ChIP-seq for HMGB1/H3K4me3 to confirm open chromatin configuration at S-phase genes; validate STMN1-dependent microtubule destabilization by immunofluorescence during mitotic progression in cycling B-cell precursors.

programme_name: Chromatin remodelling and translation machinery priming
functional_description: This programme coordinates active transcriptional and translational capacity in rapidly proliferating B-cell progenitors through concurrent upregulation of nucleosome-associated proteins (HMGN1/2, HMGB1) that promote open chromatin architecture, core proteasomal machinery (PSMA4), and RNA processing/binding factors (HNRNPA1/A2B1, LSM5). The co-expression of microtubule dynamics regulators (STMN1, TMSB4X) and oxidoreductase activity (GLRX) supports both cell division and protein quality control.
key_evidence: HMGN1/2 & HMGB1: Diagnostic markers of transcriptionally active chromatin state required during rapid G1/S transition in cycling progenitors
STMN1 & TMSB4X: Microtubule/actin dynamics proteins essential for mitotic spindle assembly and cytokinesis in Pro-B Cycling (29.5%) and Large Pre-B (40%) populations
HNRNPA1/A2B1 & LSM5: RNA processing machinery enabling rapid synthesis of cell-cycle checkpoint proteins and pre-BCR signalling components
PSMA4 & GLRX: Proteasomal degradation and protein redox balance supporting removal of misfolded proteins during high translational flux
PTMA: Apoptosis inhibitor providing survival signal during metabolically demanding proliferative phase
suggested_validation: Co-immunofluorescence of HMGN1/STMN1 with Ki67 and phospho-histone H3 on sorted Pro-B cycling and Large Pre-B populations to confirm coordinated upregulation during active cell cycle progression; correlate feature activation intensity with BrdU incorporation kinetics.

programme_name: Proliferative chromatin remodeling and microtubule dynamics
functional_description: This programme coordinates active chromatin remodeling with cell cycle machinery during B-cell proliferation. The feature is driven by high-mobility-group (HMG) nucleosome-binding proteins (HMGN1/2, HMGB1/2) that facilitate transcriptionally permissive chromatin, combined with microtubule structural proteins (TUBA1B, TUBB) required for mitotic spindle assembly. Co-expression of stathmin (STMN1), a microtubule-destabilizing protein, and histone variants (H3F3A, H2AFZ, H2AFV) indicates active replication-coupled chromatin remodeling characteristic of cycling B-cell precursors.
key_evidence: HMGN1/HMGN2: Non-histone chromatin proteins that mark transcriptionally active, accessible chromatin—diagnostic of proliferative B-cell precursors
HMGB1/HMGB2: HMG-box proteins promote nucleosome dynamics and facilitate transcription factor access during active proliferation
STMN1: Microtubule catastrophe promoter essential for G2/M transition and mitotic spindle checkpoint control
TUBA1B/TUBB: Tubulin heterodimers are rate-limiting for mitotic apparatus assembly in cycling cells
H3F3A, H2AFZ, H2AFV: Histone variants incorporated during active replication; H2AFZ marks nucleosome-depleted regions at active promoters
PTMA: Prothymosin-alpha stabilizes microtubule dynamics and suppresses apoptosis—supporting pro-proliferative state in cycling precursors
suggested_validation: Perform chromatin accessibility profiling (ATAC-seq) on FACS-sorted Pro-B/Pre-B cells with high vs. low Feature 1579 activity, followed by live-cell imaging of microtubule dynamics (EB1-GFP tracking) to confirm coordinated chromatin remodeling and mitotic spindle assembly.

programme_name: MHC Class II antigen presentation and B-cell activation
functional_description: This programme represents mature and immature B cells specialized in antigen presentation through coordinated upregulation of HLA class II molecules (DR, DP, DQ heterodimers) and associated peptide-loading machinery (CD74, HLA-DM). The programme is coupled with B-cell receptor signalling competence (CD79A, BANK1) and lymphoid homing capacity (GPR183), reflecting activated B cells engaged in or preparing for T-cell help-dependent responses.
key_evidence: CD74: Invariant chain essential for HLA class II assembly, trafficking, and peptide loading—diagnostic of active antigen-presenting B cells
HLA-DRA/DRB1/DPA1/DPB1/DQA1/DQB1: Complete HLA class II gene set (DR, DP, DQ) coordinately upregulated, indicating professional APC state
HLA-DMB: Peptide editor for class II molecules—only upregulated when B cells are actively engaged in antigen presentation
BANK1: B-cell-specific scaffold protein in BCR signalling—validates that these are signalling-competent B cells, not anergic or exhausted
MS4A1 (CD20): Pan-B-cell marker confirming feature activation is B-cell autonomous, not stromal-mediated
GPR183 (EBI2): Lymphoid-homing receptor upregulated upon EBV-driven B-cell activation, indicating recent antigen encounter or activation state
suggested_validation: Sort mature B cells by CD74/HLA-DR surface expression, perform RNA-seq to confirm coordinated HLA class II and peptide-loading gene upregulation, then co-culture with autologous CD4+ T cells to validate functional antigen presentation capacity and T-cell proliferation.

programme_name: Pro-B cell cycle progression and mitotic spindle organization
functional_description: This feature marks rapidly cycling pro-B cells characterized by active microtubule dynamics (STMN1, TUBA1B, TUBB) and mitotic spindle assembly, coupled with transcriptionally permissive chromatin architecture (HMGB1/2, HMGN1/2, H3F3A, H2AFZ). The coordinated upregulation of tubulin polymerization regulators with nucleosome remodeling factors indicates a pro-B population actively traversing S/G2/M phases during V(D)J recombination-competent development.
key_evidence: STMN1: Stathmin directly regulates microtubule catastrophe and is a canonical cell-cycle phase marker, especially enriched in S/G2/M
TUBA1B + TUBB: Tubulin alpha/beta dimers are essential for spindle pole formation and cytokinesis; their coordinated upregulation indicates active mitosis
HMGB1/2 + HMGN1/2: Non-histone architectural proteins that maintain transcriptionally open chromatin during rapid proliferation, enabling simultaneous cell-cycle and developmental gene expression
H3F3A + H2AFZ: Histone variants incorporated during active replication and at transcription sites; mark replicating chromatin in S-phase
PTMA: Prothymosin-alpha protects against apoptosis during S-phase checkpoint transitions and is upregulated in actively dividing cells
83.5% Pro-B Cycling annotation: Direct alignment with the dominant cell-type composition confirms identification of cycling pro-B stage
suggested_validation: Live-cell imaging of BM-derived pro-B cells (sorted CD19+ CD10+ IgM-) pulsed with BrdU or EdU to quantify S-phase fraction and correlate feature score with DNA synthesis rate; FACS-based mitotic index quantification (phospho-histone H3) in feature-high vs feature-low pro-B populations

programme_name: Pro-B cell S/G2/M checkpoint and chromatin remodelling
functional_description: This programme is active in rapidly cycling Pro-B cells (63.5% of top activators) and represents coordinated upregulation of chromatin dynamics, microtubule/spindle apparatus proteins, and nuclear organisation factors required for active DNA replication and mitotic progression. The dominant genes (HMGB1/2, HMGN1/2, H2A variants, H3F3A) reflect transcriptionally permissive chromatin architecture with dynamic histone exchange, while STMN1, TUBA1B, TUBB coordinate microtubule assembly for mitotic spindle formation. UBB, PTMA, and actin sequestering proteins (TMSB4X) provide structural support for cytokinesis.
key_evidence: HMGB1/HMGB2: High-mobility-group proteins facilitate chromatin accessibility and are hallmarks of active, proliferating cells in S/G2/M phase
HMGN1/HMGN2: Nucleosome-binding proteins associated with transcriptionally active chromatin; upregulated during replication
STMN1: Microtubule-destabilising protein (stathmin) essential for spindle checkpoint control and mitotic fidelity
TUBA1B/TUBB: α/β-tubulin dimers are rate-limiting for spindle apparatus assembly; their coordinate upregulation indicates active M-phase entry
H2AFZ/H2AFV/H2AFY: Histone variants enable nucleosome remodelling and are enriched during S-phase chromatin replication
PTMA: Prothymosin-α inhibits apoptosis and enables proliferation in stressed proliferating cells
suggested_validation: Co-immunofluorescence staining of Pro-B enriched populations (CD34+/CD19+) for phospho-H3 (mitotic marker) with STMN1/HMGB1 to confirm this feature marks the S/G2/M cycling subpopulation; validate by flow cytometry sorting on STMN1 expression and Hoechst/EdU incorporation to confirm enrichment in active DNA synthesis phases

programme_name: Mature B cell MHC-II antigen presentation programme
functional_description: This feature represents a coordinated programme of MHC class II and antigen presentation machinery upregulation in mature B cells. The dominant signature includes all classical HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ heterodimer components (α and β chains) along with CD74 (invariant chain), establishing functional antigen presentation capability. Co-expression of B-cell identity markers (MS4A1/CD20, CD79A, BANK1) and GPR183 (EBV-responsive chemokine receptor) indicates this programme is activated in mature B cells engaged in antigen sensing and presentation functions.
key_evidence: CD74: Invariant chain essential for MHC-II assembly and trafficking; diagnostic for antigen-presenting B cells
HLA-DRA/DRB1/DPA1/DPB1/DQA1/DQB1: Complete MHC-II presentation machinery; coordinately upregulated indicates active antigen presentation state
MS4A1/CD20 + CD79A: B-cell lineage markers; 79.5% mature B composition confirms mature B cell identity
BANK1: B-cell-specific scaffolding protein in BCR signalling; indicates activated B cell state compatible with antigen presentation
GPR183: Chemokine receptor upregulated on EBV-infected and antigen-activated B cells; marker of antigen-experienced B cells
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry: Sort feature-high B cells and quantify surface MHC-II (HLA-DR) and CD80/CD86 co-stimulatory molecule expression; perform functional antigen presentation assay using autologous T cell proliferation with peptide-pulsed feature-high vs feature-low B cells as APCs

programme_name: ER chaperone-mediated Ig folding and ERAD
functional_description: This programme coordinates endoplasmic reticulum protein quality control during active immunoglobulin synthesis, combining PDI-family disulfide isomerases (PDIA6, P4HB), HSP70/HSP90 chaperones (HSPA5, HSP90B1), and ER-resident cofactors (SDF2L1, CALR) for heavy and light chain folding. Concurrent ERAD machinery activation (UBE2J1, DAD1) supports clearance of misfolded Ig, essential for maintaining secretory capacity in plasma cells and pro-B cycling cells undergoing Ig recombination.
key_evidence: PDIA6: PDI family member catalysing disulfide bond isomerisation—core mechanism for correct Ig domain folding
HSPA5 (BiP): ER-resident HSP70 chaperone essential for nascent Ig chain binding and ERAD substrate recognition
HSP90B1: ER-localised HSP90 supporting late-stage Ig domain stabilisation and client protein maturation
P4HB: Prolyl 4-hydroxylase with dual chaperone and catalytic activity for collagen-like Ig stabilisation
SDF2L1: ER-resident cofactor enabling refolding of transiently misfolded Ig intermediates
CALR: Calreticulin serving as glycoprotein chaperone and ER Ca2+ regulator supporting Ig folding
UBE2J1: E2 ubiquitin conjugase directing proteasomal degradation of irreversibly misfolded Ig
DAD1: ERAD-associated component protecting membrane integrity during protein translocation and degradation
suggested_validation: Perform selective immunoprecipitation of newly synthesized IgG from feature-high plasma cells treated with proteasome inhibitor MG132, then quantify polyubiquitinated Ig intermediates by Western blot; compare PDIA6/HSPA5/UBE2J1 dependency using CRISPR screens on plasma cell maturation and Ig secretion capacity.

programme_name: Ribosomal protein synthesis and nucleotide metabolism
functional_description: This feature represents a proliferative programme centred on ribosomal biogenesis and active protein translation machinery, enriched in cycling Large Pre-B cells undergoing clonal expansion. The co-expression of nucleotide metabolism enzymes (DUT), ubiquitin-proteasome system components (UBB), and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation proteins (UQCRQ, UQCRH) indicates coordinated anabolic and energy metabolism supporting rapid cell division. The presence of 20.5% plasma cells suggests that actively secreting cells also engage this translation programme to support Ig production, though the dominant signal is proliferative.
key_evidence: RPLP0, RPS17, RPL37A, RPS24, RPS23: Five ribosomal protein genes in top 15 diagnostic of active translation machinery required for rapid protein synthesis during B-cell proliferation
DUT: Nucleotide metabolism enzyme enabling dNTP and dUMP supply for DNA replication and concurrent translation demand in cycling cells
UBB: Ubiquitin system component necessary for selective protein turnover during cell cycle progression and quality control during rapid Ig synthesis
UQCRQ, UQCRH: Mitochondrial complex III subunits indicating elevated oxidative phosphorylation to fuel proliferative anabolism
STMN1, TMSB4X: Cytoskeletal regulatory proteins supporting dynamic morphology changes required for mitosis
suggested_validation: Sort Large Pre-B cells (CD34−CD19+CD10+) and plasma cells (CD38hiCD27+) separately; perform polysome profiling and pulse-chase labelling of newly synthesized proteins to confirm elevated translation flux is primary in Pre-B cycling subsets versus sustained in plasma cells, and correlate feature activation with Ki-67+ cycling cells by flow cytometry.

programme_name: HSC/LMPP ribosomal protein synthesis programme
functional_description: This feature represents coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins (RPS2, RPS17, RPS23, RPS24, RPL4, RPL7A, RPLP0) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) in long-term HSCs and LMPPs, reflecting their high biosynthetic capacity for maintaining stemness and self-renewal. The co-expression of HSP90AB1 (chaperone), NPM1 (nucleolar/centrosomal protein), and iron metabolism genes (FTH1) indicates a tightly coordinated translational programme supporting rapid cell division and organelle biogenesis in uncommitted progenitors.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS2, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: six ribosomal proteins spanning both 40S and 60S subunits indicate global translational upregulation, not specific to plasma cell secretion
EEF1B2: elongation factor essential for basal translation elongation, diagnostic of proliferative rather than specialised secretory programme
